recovered_habits.boundary_condition: If the obligation is optional, remote, explicitly flexible, or the current itinerary still has a real cushion, the user will consider the leaner or cheaper option.
recovered_habits.default_action: Choose the earlier nonstop, previous-day arrival, later return, or extra hotel night when needed to avoid sprinting or risking the first/last obligation.

evidence.quote: The Tuesday start is 10:00 a.m., so I don’t want to cut it close.
I do not love leaving before lunch, but missing a 3:00 setup would be worse.
I don’t love giving up the afternoon flight, but for this one I’d rather not gamble on a connection or land rushed.
Let’s do the calmer version: Sunday in, Friday home.
Let’s not do the Thursday sprint. Book the Friday morning return.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: The user may accept a tighter plan only after consciously accepting the risk and keeping baggage/ground logistics lean; comfort alone is not enough to add nights.
recovered_habits.name: Protect fixed-event buffers over convenience and small savings
recovered_habits.preference_value: For schedule-sensitive trainings, certifications, client setup windows, equipment handoffs, and debriefs, the user prefers itinerary buffer over a cheaper fare, a later departure, or avoiding an extra hotel night.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Work or certification travel with fixed start times, setup/calibration/handoff windows, checked equipment, or uncertain end times.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A one-stop itinerary is acceptable when nonstop fares are unreasonable, no nonstop exists, or the fare difference is meaningfully large.
recovered_habits.default_action: Start with nonstop options; if connecting, use one comfortable layover and avoid tight or long connections, especially with holidays, weather, or equipment.

evidence.quote: United is fine when it’s basically tied, but I care more about a simple route and not sitting through some long connection. One short layover is okay; two is not worth it.
I’d rather take a nonstop from Denver if it’s reasonable; one short layover is okay if the fare difference is big. No two-stop stuff.
I’m okay with a connection, just not a two-stop mess or a layover that eats half the day.
I’m fine with one connection, but I don’t want two stops or some long sit. United is fine if it works, but schedule matters more.
I don’t want a two-hour airport sit just to save $90.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Do not pick a worse connection merely for a preferred airline or small savings.
recovered_habits.name: Prefer nonstops and simple routing over carrier loyalty
recovered_habits.preference_value: The user prefers nonstop flights or simple one-stop itineraries, with schedule reliability more important than airline loyalty. One reasonable layover is acceptable when needed or when savings are large; two stops, long sits, and brittle connections are disfavored.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Flights from Denver for work, family, and leisure trips.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: The user does not require premium cabins; price sensitivity remains within regular economy.
recovered_habits.default_action: Book regular economy/main cabin rather than basic economy, then select seats during or soon after booking.

evidence.quote: Avoid basic economy, and keep the hotel cancellable if possible.
Main cabin, not basic. I’ll carry on.
Economy but not basic.
United or Southwest would both be okay. I just don’t want basic economy because I need normal seat selection and a carry-on.
Economy with seat selection. Not basic. And if there are decent window seats, grab those.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: On low-cost carriers, the user may buy carry-on and seat selection à la carte if the total remains worthwhile.
recovered_habits.name: Book regular economy/main cabin, not basic economy
recovered_habits.preference_value: Coach/economy is fine, but the user wants normal seat selection, carry-on rights, and standard flexibility; basic economy is normally avoided.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Air ticketing for solo work travel and couple/family trips where seat choice and carry-on access matter.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Do not split companions merely to get a better window; modest seat fees are acceptable, but silly fees are not.
recovered_habits.default_action: Select/request a window for the user when available; for companion trips, choose adjacent seats with at least one window if practical.

evidence.quote: Window seat if there’s a decent one, not an exit row.
If you can request a window, do it, just not an exit row.
For Frontier I’m just doing backpack plus carry-on. If a window seat is under about $25, grab it. If it’s silly, I’ll risk check-in.
And if there’s a window with the two of us together, great, but don’t split us up for it.
Let’s do around 2:30, same flight for both of us. Window for me if there’s a decent pair together; Mark does not care.
For seats, same as Indy: window if it is not the last row, aisle over a last-row window, and no middle.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If the only window is poor, take an aisle over a last-row window or middle seat; avoid exit rows unless explicitly acceptable.
recovered_habits.name: Window-seat preference with practical limits
recovered_habits.preference_value: The user prefers a decent window seat, but avoids exit rows, last-row/no-recline compromises, and middle seats. When traveling with a spouse/companion, sitting together outranks getting the perfect window.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Flight seat selection for both solo and companion travel.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A hotel can be practical/basic if reviews are acceptable and logistics are strong; luxury is not required.
recovered_habits.default_action: Screen out poorly reviewed hotels and choose a solid, comfortable property rather than the lowest-rate option.

evidence.quote: I’d rather not use a poorly reviewed hotel, so think 4.0-plus if possible.
But I don’t want a sketchy low-rated place. Around 4 stars or better, and I need a gym.
For hotels, I don’t need fancy, but keep it well reviewed, four-ish or better if possible.
For hotels, keep it to 4.0-plus reviews if possible.
I’m fine losing the hot tub if the rest is cleaner. I do not want a sketchy 3.6-rated place just because it has parking.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Do not choose a low-rated property just because it has parking, a hot tub, or a lower price.
recovered_habits.name: Use a hotel quality floor around 4.0+ reviews
recovered_habits.preference_value: The user wants well-reviewed hotels, usually around 4.0+ guest rating or better, and avoids sketchy or depressing bargain properties even when not seeking luxury.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel selection for work trips, family trips, and leisure weekends.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Commute, parking, review quality, and schedule reliability can override the hot tub or pool.
recovered_habits.default_action: Prefer hotels that have fitness access and, when feasible, pool/hot tub amenities; confirm amenity hours when they matter.

evidence.quote: Gym matters, pool or hot tub would be nice.
For hotels I care about good reviews and a real gym; pool or hot tub would be a plus for the weekend.
For hotels, I’d like 4.0 or better if possible, and pool/hot tub/gym would be useful after training days.
Pool or fitness would be nice; hot tub is a bonus, not the whole trip.
I use a gym or pool if it is there, and a hot tub is nice, but not worth a silly commute.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: For leisure recovery weekends, hot tub/pool/balcony amenities may carry more weight, but still not enough to justify a bad commute or nonrefundable overpay by default.
recovered_habits.name: Hotel amenities hierarchy: gym first, pool useful, hot tub/soaking optional
recovered_habits.preference_value: A usable fitness room or real gym is a recurring priority; pool access is useful, and a hot tub/soaking option is valued for recovery but is normally a bonus rather than the deciding factor.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel selection across work trips and leisure stays, especially after standing-heavy training days or hiking weekends.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A farther hotel can win only if the work commute remains reasonable or if a confirmed spouse/weekend extension changes the purpose of the stay.
recovered_habits.default_action: Choose the suburban/near-site hotel that shortens workday drives and simplifies parking/loading, even if it lacks a hot tub or downtown feel.

evidence.quote: Let’s not add a half hour of driving for a hot tub.
For this one I care more about rating and not being stranded for dinner than the hot tub. Pool and fitness are enough if the commute is short.
For hotels, shortest commute wins once we know the site.
I don’t want to commute from the wrong side of town for three mornings.
I’ll have the demo analyzer and a couple workbook boxes, so I care a lot more about simple parking than restaurants.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: After the work portion, the user may switch to a more leisure-oriented hotel if the upside is real and expenses stay separated.
recovered_habits.name: For work hotels, prioritize commute, parking, and gear handling over downtown or hot tub appeal
recovered_habits.preference_value: On work trips, the user prefers a hotel close to the actual site or central to the clinic loop, with easy parking/unloading, over a downtown location, better restaurant scene, or hot tub.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Client training, rollout, calibration, and multi-site work trips, especially with demo cases or workbooks.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Multiple holds are acceptable only if cancellation deadlines are clear and the user will not forget to release extras.
recovered_habits.default_action: Hold cancellable rooms, track deadlines, and avoid prepaid rates; use duplicate holds only when necessary and manageable.

evidence.quote: Avoid basic economy, and keep the hotel cancellable if possible.
Good. Don’t book anything prepaid.
Can I hold two cancellable hotels without making a mess?
I also don’t want to float three reservations and then forget to cancel something.
Yes, lock the cancellable Sedona room. Don’t pay for a guaranteed view if it makes the rate nonrefundable.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Do not pay for a guaranteed view/balcony if it makes the rate nonrefundable unless explicitly reapproved.
recovered_habits.name: Prefer cancellable/refundable lodging and avoid prepaid locks while plans are uncertain
recovered_habits.preference_value: The user strongly prefers cancellable/refundable hotel rates and avoids prepaid/nonrefundable bookings when schedules, spouse participation, or site locations are uncertain.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel reservations, split stays, backup holds, and leisure rooms with uncertain timing or amenities.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A one-day rental may be considered for a specific leisure day trip, but not a full-stay rental when hotel parking is expensive.
recovered_habits.default_action: Skip the rental for city-center conferences and use rideshare/taxi/transit; rent when sites, gear, or family logistics make independence valuable.

evidence.quote: I do not want a rental car unless Seattle makes that foolish.
I would rather not rent a car unless it’s clearly useful. I’ll have a backpack and maybe one small kit, not the big demo case.
No rental. I’ll rideshare with the demo gear.
Rental car seems unavoidable, right? Lab, hotel, dinner, and St. Paul maybe later are all spread out.
Okay. I need a rental car then, right? I wondered about rideshares, but with the analyzer that sounds annoying.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If demo/analyzer cases, workbook cartons, multiple clinics, or uncertain pickups are involved, rental becomes the default.
recovered_habits.name: Rent cars only when operationally useful; otherwise use rideshare/transit
recovered_habits.preference_value: The user does not want a rental car by default. For urban conference stays, she prefers rideshare/transit; for multi-site suburbs, equipment, unreliable family pickups, or spread-out logistics, she rents a car.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Ground transportation decisions for work conferences, clinic loops, family trips, and spouse leisure extensions.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A standard SUV is acceptable when spouse gear or additional cartons justify it; a compact/midsize car is fine only for light personal trips.
recovered_habits.default_action: Reserve the smallest SUV/crossover class that reliably fits the case/cartons and is practical for garages/parking.

evidence.quote: Rental car: compact SUV or midsize? I need room for the case and demo materials, but one clinic has a tight garage.
Rental car: sedan or small SUV? The analyzer case is basically a chunky Pelican case, plus two cartons if shipping fails.
Book the compact SUV too. I need enough room for two cartons and the demo laptop case, but I do not want something oversized.
Standard SUV, with midsize SUV as fallback. No sedan unless there’s no choice and you ask me.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Do not substitute a sedan for gear-heavy trips without asking; avoid a huge SUV unless inventory or cargo volume requires it.
recovered_habits.name: Choose SUV/crossover class for gear, not sedan; avoid oversizing unless needed
recovered_habits.preference_value: When transporting demo/analyzer cases, cartons, or family gear, the user prefers a compact/midsize/standard SUV or crossover with easy loading rather than a sedan; she also avoids unnecessarily oversized vehicles.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Rental car class selection for clinic rollouts, equipment travel, and family trips with extra cargo.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: One move can be acceptable; multiple or low-value moves are avoided.
recovered_habits.default_action: Prefer one continuous hotel when it does not harm logistics; split only after work obligations or when it materially improves work mornings/weekend value; keep folios/cards/receipts separate.

evidence.quote: Would you split it or stay put? I hate changing hotels on work trips unless the upside is real.
That difference is fine. I’ll expense the Wednesday/Thursday part and cover the weekend upgrade personally if needed.
I don’t mind moving hotels if it actually improves the weekend.
How should I split this so accounting doesn’t get weird?
If Mark comes, I would rather not change hotels Friday.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If repacking/bag handling would create friction and the benefit is marginal, stay put.
recovered_habits.name: Avoid hotel moves on work trips unless the upside is real; separate business and personal pieces
recovered_habits.preference_value: The user dislikes changing hotels during work trips, but will split stays when the work/weekend or logistics upside is meaningful. She wants business and personal costs clearly separated.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Work trips with spouse/weekend extensions, conference-to-weekend transitions, or changing work locations.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Alternate airports or cheaper routings remain candidates only when net savings are substantial and the drive/weather/timing is acceptable.
recovered_habits.default_action: Pay a modest premium for the simpler or more reliable option when the net savings shrink after logistics are included.

evidence.quote: Assume my brother says no pickups after 10:30. Does the airport hotel kill the savings?
Fares already look uneven, and I’m wondering whether we should fly into Milwaukee or use Chicago and rent a car.
Even with the fare difference? It’s about $310 more total for the two of us.
The Santa Fe nonstop is running about $180 more per person than the Albuquerque option once I include the rental. That still feels annoying.
Milwaukee if at all possible. I do not want to add O’Hare and a rental drive to a holiday week unless the savings are ridiculous.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If savings become truly large or budget is the controlling factor, the user will reconsider the less convenient option.
recovered_habits.name: Evaluate total trip cost and hassle, not just headline fare
recovered_habits.preference_value: The user compares door-to-door package cost and hassle, including rental cars, hotels, parking, tolls, pickups, and late arrivals. Small savings are not worth added driving, alternate airports, hotels, or misconnect risk.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Choosing between airports, flight times, connections, late arrivals, and hotel/car packages for work, family, and leisure trips.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Fixed pieces such as a definite destination flight or cancellable hotel may be held earlier if fares/rooms are at risk.
recovered_habits.default_action: Ask the coordinator/client targeted questions and use conditional branches or cancellable holds until the key logistics are confirmed.

evidence.quote: What exactly should I ask the client before I book?
Let us not book until they confirm Tuesday. What exactly should I ask the client by Friday?
And what questions do I send the client so we can stop maintaining two plans?
What client details should I ask before I book anything nonrefundable?
Before I commit, give me the confirmation questions for the coordinator. Include whether I actually need to be in Stockton Thursday.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Do not lock tight returns, site-dependent hotels, or nonrefundable rooms while Thursday/Friday obligations, addresses, or equipment handling remain unresolved.
recovered_habits.name: Confirm work-trip operational details before locking nonrefundable pieces
recovered_habits.preference_value: For work travel, the user wants exact operational details before finalizing nonrefundable or hard-to-change bookings: site order, start/end times, setup/handoff requirements, parking/loading, storage, and gear/shipping responsibilities.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Client trainings, analyzer rollouts, certification labs, and multi-site clinic trips with uncertain schedules or equipment.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Checked bags/cases are used when equipment, consumables, family luggage, or long trips require them.
recovered_habits.default_action: Use carry-on plus backpack/tote where possible; if checking equipment, keep laptop, chargers, medication, handouts, adapters, and must-have demo pieces with her.

evidence.quote: No checked bag. Carry-on and backpack.
No checked bags, just carry-ons.
Carry-on plus backpack is fine.
Help me keep this carry-on only.
I want carry-on only if possible.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: When a first-day schedule is tight, avoid checked personal bags unless operationally necessary.
recovered_habits.name: Carry-on personal luggage when feasible; check only required gear and keep essentials with her
recovered_habits.preference_value: The user prefers carry-on-only personal travel when feasible, especially for conferences and tight arrivals. Checked baggage is acceptable for demo/training cases or consumables, but critical items should remain in the carry-on/personal item.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Packing and baggage decisions for flights, especially with certification check-ins, weather, or equipment risk.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: The user will not pay nonrefundable or excessive premiums merely for a view/balcony, and family-event logistics or budget can shift the hotel choice more practical.
recovered_habits.default_action: Hold/request cancellable resort, oceanfront, lodge, or recovery-style rooms; plan reasonable arrival/return times and avoid over-scheduled or driving-heavy weekends.

evidence.quote: We want restaurants without driving if possible, light hiking, a comfortable room, and some kind of pool or soaking option. I don’t want a poorly reviewed bargain.
Hotel matters more than usual: solid guest reviews, comfortable room, hot tub or pool and a gym if we can get them. Balcony would be nice, not mandatory.
Beach access and strong reviews matter. A balcony would be great. Hot tub would be nice after hiking, but I don’t want to turn the weekend into a driving project.
Recovery weekend, but not luxury for the sake of it. Friday evening arrival feels like it cuts too much out. I like the balcony-room idea; he cares more about hot tub and easy parking.

I want either a true oceanfront/boardwalk stay or something closer to family in Chesapeake. I’d like the guest rating to be at least around 4.0. Pool and fitness room matter; hot tub is nice but not a deal breaker. Balcony if we do oceanfront.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If the weekend is primarily family obligations rather than a getaway, location and logistics can outweigh resort amenities.
recovered_habits.name: For spouse leisure weekends, choose restorative lodging and avoid turning the trip into logistics
recovered_habits.preference_value: For personal weekends with her spouse, the user wants the trip to feel restorative: strong reviews, comfortable room, beach/resort/scenic feel, pool or hot tub when possible, fitness access, easy parking, and balcony/patio as a nice-to-have.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Anniversary, beach, Santa Fe, Oregon Coast, Sedona, and similar spouse leisure weekends or work-plus-weekend extensions.
